title: Supervisory tiers narrate per-step progress to the main interactive thread, burning the owner's finite session budget with information they did not ask for and cannot act on
description: Owner-reported, and reported for the SECOND time - the same feedback was given in a prior session and did not stick, which is itself the evidence that guidance is the wrong instrument here. MECHANISM: supervisory tiers (Tier 0 Mind, Tier 1 Orchestrator, Tier 2 Coordinator) relay per-step progress, lane-start announcements and running status updates INTO THE MAIN INTERACTIVE THREAD. The main thread is a HUMAN-FACING RELAY SEAT, not a supervisory bus: its only legitimate functions are issuing owner rulings and relaying finished outcomes. THREE DISTINCT COSTS, and the third is the one that ends sessions. (1) It burns the OWNER'S context with information they did not ask for. Standing owner directive 5 is explicit: no status reports unless asked, silence is the correct output when work is proceeding. (2) The information is UNACTIONABLE at that seat - a lane-start announcement or a mid-flight status line gives the owner nothing to decide, because the decision it would inform belongs to the tier that sent it. Directive 4: the owner walks away for hours and will not read a live feed; problems become RECORDED DEFECTS, not chat. (3) It COMPETES FOR THE SAME FINITE SESSION BUDGET WHOSE EXHAUSTION KILLED THE PREVIOUS FLEET. This is not an aesthetic complaint about verbosity. The fleet that died at approximately 14:15Z did not degrade as it approached the API session limit - it ran at full concurrency until the API refused and every agent died at once, several mid-write. Every token of unrequested narration spent in the main thread was budget unavailable to the work, and the main thread was THE PRINCIPAL OFFENDER in that session. Method canon rule from the same engagement applies directly: BUDGET, NOT WALL-CLOCK, IS THE CONSTRAINT. CORRECT BEHAVIOUR: peer-to-peer messaging between agents for coordination; recorded defects and backlog items for problems; the main thread receives a SINGLE finished synthesis at terminal state, or an escalation that genuinely requires an owner ruling, and nothing else.

context.relationship_to_prior: STRENGTHENING, NOT DUPLICATE. This entry records the OUTBOUND direction (supervisory seats pushing narration INTO the main thread). The one prior ledger instance records the INVERSE direction and therefore does not cover it.

prior_instances.why_it_does_not_cover_this: It records the INVERSE DIRECTION - the main thread DOING WORK (copying 28 role manifests into the product repo, auditing harness source to diagnose the stagnation detector, instructing the auditor to suppress a harness-issued defect). That is inbound role-boundary violation BY the main thread. This defect is outbound narration TO the main thread by the supervisory tiers, a different actor set, a different direction, and a different cost. Verified at source by reading the archive entry rather than trusting the citation. Note it was also filed against a DIFFERENT REPO, so the class has now appeared in two repos.
prior_instances.curation_note: Curated PROCESS_OBSERVATION - agent-behaviour observation rather than a skill defect. That curation class is part of the problem: classifying a repeatable behavioural failure as an observation is what leaves it with no control attached.

prior_instances.location: docs/planning/olt-mind-resume/HANDOFF-2026-08-25.md sections 0.65-0.76, DELETED in the same commit that filed this defect
prior_instances.why_it_does_not_cover_this: Directive 4 (the main thread is not a communication channel) and directive 5 (no status reports unless asked) existed ONLY AS PROSE IN A DOCUMENT SLATED FOR DELETION and were never filed as defects or attached to any control. THIS IS WHY THE FEEDBACK HAD TO BE GIVEN TWICE. A directive whose only home is a document nobody is required to read is not in force. The directives themselves are now preserved at hb-s0-standing-owner-directives in .olt/backlog.jsonl.

contributing_cause.summary: MUCH OF THE CHATTER WAS STRUCTURALLY FORCED, NOT MERELY UNDISCIPLINED.
contributing_cause.mechanism: ListAgents is SESSION-DISABLED - error text: 'ListAgents is disabled for this session, in subagents as well as here.' olt-mind and olt-orchestrator DECLARE ListAgents on their role types and do not receive it. Supervisory seats therefore COULD NOT MEASURE THEIR OWN ROSTER, so the main thread became the only seat able to count running agents against the 8-concurrent ceiling, and EVERY DISPATCH DECISION ROUND-TRIPPED THROUGH THE OWNER SEAT. Corroborated live during the filing of this defect: orchestrator_handoff-retirement's own ListAgents call returned that exact error, and SendMessage to 'mind' returned 'No agent named mind is reachable', leaving the owner seat as the only resolvable address.
contributing_cause.implication: REMOVING THE MOTIVE IS THE BETTER HALF OF THE FIX - the same shape as f6079d51, which removed the motive for --no-verify rather than only prohibiting it. Restore roster visibility to the supervisory seats and most of the round-tripping disappears without anyone needing to be disciplined. A control on the remaining discretionary narration is the other half.

remedy.form: CONTROL, NOT GUIDANCE. Guidance on this has now FAILED TWICE - once as a standing directive in a handoff document, once as owner feedback in-session. A third restatement is predicted to fail identically.
remedy.rationale: Handoff section 9 records the argument in general form: every durable method improvement came from the tier being corrected, not from the tiers doing the correcting, and that asymmetry is THE ARGUMENT FOR GATES OVER GUIDANCE - made by the seats that were enforcing the guidance. This defect is a direct instance: the supervisory tiers are both the offender and the enforcer, so self-enforcement has no independent check.
remedy.shape_required: A mechanism that makes unrequested narration to the human relay seat REFUSABLE OR MEASURABLE rather than merely discouraged. Design is deliberately left open - specifying the control is the repair task, not this record. Whatever is chosen must be fail-closed in the sense used throughout this ledger: absence of an owner request must not render as permission to report.
remedy.acceptance_criterion: Per the standing gate rule that every gate needs a criterion a stub must fail: a control that passes when a lane sends nothing AND passes when a lane sends unrequested progress is not a control. It must discriminate between a terminal synthesis, a genuine owner-ruling escalation, and mid-flight narration.

context.filing_note: Appended by orchestrator_handoff-retirement under Tier 0 Mind mandate. Mind holds no Write tool and the harness exposes no defect:add verb at Tier 0, which is itself a gap worth noting: THE SEAT THAT OWNS THE DEFECT LEDGER CANNOT WRITE TO IT - the same shape as hb-auditor-cannot-record-its-own-findings, where mind-auditor can manufacture a defect but cannot file one.
context.shape_note: Fields match the 107-line majority shape MINUS 'curation'. Every existing statused line also carries 'curation', but that key is written by a curation pass and encodes a curator's verdict; this actor has no standing to issue one, and pre-empting it would hide the entry from the next curation sweep.

observation: Execution detected on interactive main conversation thread without subagent boundary delegation.
remediation: Main thread must not directly modify code or execute implementation tasks. Dispatch Tier 2 Background Coordinators or Tier 3 Implementers via invoke_subagent.
